> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cbfa5e43354f430e35c4f9f24732e59848174889` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3ef5c23d367d54e8bca8e47982609d3708f008bd` — the merge of head `f5a955e12a73e00e2d196e34ec16c0d1e529d12a` into base `cbfa5e43354f430e35c4f9f24732e59848174889`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3ef5c23d367d54e8bca8e47982609d3708f008bd && git checkout 3ef5c23d367d54e8bca8e47982609d3708f008bd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cbfa5e43354f430e35c4f9f24732e59848174889 f5a955e12a73e00e2d196e34ec16c0d1e529d12a && git checkout -B drift-repro cbfa5e43354f430e35c4f9f24732e59848174889 && git merge --no-ff f5a955e12a73e00e2d196e34ec16c0d1e529d12a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cbfa5e43354f430e35c4f9f24732e59848174889
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cbfa5e43354f430e35c4f9f24732e59848174889` → pass the list as

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · PR #24248 at `f5a955e12` (#23217 slice 1) · review of record for the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` export

`domain:cli` seat 2 · `marchtian` · session `session_01QyoWKK9RwUNxBxmevy9Neb` · 2026-10-18T02:53Z · holder of claim 6244297836 · `Ruling-ref: 6227928430` (letter A). The dev's report is comment 6244895373 on #23217. The seat read the new module in full and reviewed against this PR, not the report's own account. Per `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier`, a `Clause-②: yes` declaration with no published-schema face is owed the lane seat's own review at `TIER_DEFAULT`; this record is that review.

1. **Shape.** Draft → `main`. The first line is `Part of #23217` (four doors remain), and there is no closing keyword. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Ruling-ref: 6227928430` are line-initial, and the assignee is `marchtian`. 8 files, +1055 / −231. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 24248`: NOT governed.
2. **The export (the review of record).** The export is `resolveRequestExecutionContext(input: RequestExecutionContextInput)` from core's `.` entry (through `security/index.ts`, beside `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture`, as letter A item 1 places it), with the types `RequestAuthService`, `EstablishedRequestSession` and `RequestAdmission`. Read against the letter and the card's amended scope:
   - **Name:** it says what it returns. The guest overload returns `Promise<ExecutionContext>` and the general one `Promise<ExecutionContext | undefined>`, so the fail-closed `undefined` is in the type.
   - **The two choices, made once and documented:** `anonymous: 'fail-closed' | 'guest'` and `authGate: 'withhold' | 'resolved' | 'reread-when-active'`. A gate re-read that fails is `AuthzStoreUnavailableError('auth_gate')`, never a silent drop. That is the contract-first, loud-on-fault shape the anti-AI-error axis asks for.
   - **Every door difference is a REQUIRED named parameter** (11, with 0 item-5 fallbacks; the dev's door table is in the PR body). A door with no value passes `undefined` or the withholding literal, so a door, or an AI writing one, cannot drop an input by omitting a key. The past copies each lost an input by omission (#15351, #15352, #22258, #15747), so this blocks that failure class by construction.
   - **Dependency direction (H4):** core imports only `@objectstack/spec` types and `@objectstack/types` (`inProcessSessionReadInput`; already a dependency), plus its own security modules. The OAuth verification and scope reading stay at the runtime door, because they need `@objectstack/spec/ai` (H2).
   - **Faults propagate:** nothing is caught around the resolver. The one swallow is a session read that throws, which reads as no session, exactly as the doors read it before.
   - **No app-author surface:** this is a platform-door seam, as ruling C′ item 3 and letter A keep it.
3. **The runtime door, read on the diff.** It keeps only what is its own (service lookups, header normalisation, the `/mcp` OAuth verification and scope reading) and calls the function: −209 / +86. Its 39 pins and #24137's 15 OAuth pins stay green unchanged. The ruling-item-4 conformance test (`request-execution-context.conformance.test.ts`, 7 cases) has one row per converted door, with a CONTROL case. The dev notes that the conformance equalities stay green under an ablation of the function by construction, because both sides call it; the CONTROL case and the 20-case core unit battery are what catch a defect in the function.
4. **Evidence.**
   - Ablation of choice 1 (always fail-closed), with the restore proven by blob: core "Tests 1 failed | 19 passed (20)" and runtime "Tests 10 failed | 36 passed (46)" (9 door pins plus the conformance CONTROL), in the declared direction.
   - Core local: 104 files, 2551 passed. Runtime local: 413 files, 6318 passed. Both typechecks exit 0 with their debt ledgers unchanged.
   - Gates: 84 derived, 83 run, all exit 0. One was NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (needs a whole-tree build), which is CI's. `check:authz-resolver`, `check:published-files`, `check:dts-closure` and `check:lean-entry-closure` all exit 0. ESLint `--no-inline-config` exited 0.
5. **Changeset, read sentence by sentence.** `@objectstack/core` `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, as letter A prescribes.
   - The new-export bullet names the four exports above.
   - The two-choices bullet and the named-parameters bullet match the module.
   - "First caller … What that door answers is unchanged" matches the door pins.
   - "Faults propagate" matches the code.
   - No `@objectstack/runtime` changeset: its door's answers do not move, and the refactor is described where a reader looks for it.
6. **Cross-lane:**
   - Engine seat: `6244304634` plus the addendum `6244918458` (`authz-store-unavailable.test.ts`'s ledger row).
   - Spec seat: `6244914013` (`scripts/check-single-authz-resolver.mjs`'s `DELEGATORS`). This re-points an existing gate's reader so it cannot pass vacuously; it is not a new gate.
7. **Accepted deviations:**
   - the two out-of-surface files, as in item 6;
   - the ablation of choice 1 instead of the gate, because the runtime door withholds the gate and a gate ablation could not redden any door pin;
   - the door's single `auth` lookup moved ahead of the tenancy read: identical answers for any lookup that resolves or rejects, and the dispatcher's `resolveService` never throws synchronously. This is in the PR's Acceptance notes;
   - the signature in the PR body written with guillemets, which the sanitizer requires;
   - `origin/main` moved after the merge, on unrelated `rest` files.
8. **Out of scope, noted:** #23217's title ("not a published export") and its scope item 3 still read as ruling C′ wrote them, while letter A amended item 1 to an export from core's `.` entry. The ruling record `6227928430` governs. The card text is left to the director seat that wrote it, and later slices' orders quote letter A. The `handover_slice2` list (REST's `computeExecCtx`, with `fail-closed` / `reread-when-active` / `required` / `withhold`) is the next slice's start.
9. **Landing.** Ordinary queue landing once every check on `f5a955e12` is green or a roster skip and no objection stands on #6017 or #6367. `Part of` closes nothing: the seat posts the landed note on #23217, and slice 2 is claimed after this merges.
